item.title: Industrial Growth Series: Why Great Industrial Companies Stop Growing
item.description:
Monday, August 24, 2026 at 12 PM

Location: Ion, 4201 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Register here: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/1996106693855?aff=oddtdtcreator Great industrial companies do not usually stop growing because they lack capability. They stop growing because the market changes around them. For years, many industrial companies have grown through strong relationships, repeat customers, referrals, reputation, and word of mouth. That approach can work for a long time. Until it does not. The company is still strong. The team still delivers. Customers still trust the work. The reputation is still solid. But new opportunities become harder to create. The same relationships are no longer producing the same volume of business. Referrals become less predictable. Buyers become harder to reach. Competitors become more visible. The company starts depending too heavily on the momentum it built in the past. That is where many great industrial companies get stuck. They are not failing. They have simply reached a point where the way they grew before may not be enough to support where they want to go next. This session of the Industrial Growth Series is designed to help owners, executives, and commercial leaders understand why strong industrial companies hit growth ceilings and what must begin to change to create new momentum. We will explore the role of market positioning, visibility, relationships, business development, diversification, and changing buyer behavior without turning the conversation into another tactical sales seminar. This is not about chasing every opportunity. It is not about abandoning the relationships that helped build the company. It is about recognizing when the market has changed and ensuring the company’s approach to growth changes with it. What You’ll Learn Why successful industrial companies eventually hit growth ceilings Why reputation, referrals, and repeat customers may stop producing the same results How changing markets and buyer behavior affect industrial growth Where commercial momentum commonly begins to slow Why strong capabilities do not always create strong market visibility How leaders can begin creating new paths to growth What established companies should evaluate before investing in more activity Who Should Attend Industrial company owners and CEOs Manufacturing leaders Energy, oil and gas, and field service companies Construction and infrastructure firms Commercial, sales, and business development leaders Companies with strong capabilities but inconsistent new opportunity flow Leaders working to break through a growth plateau Event Format 11:45 AM – 12:00 PM | Networking at the stairs 12:00 PM – 12:40 PM | Presentation 12:40 PM – 1:00 PM | Discussion and Q&A 1:00 PM – 1:15 PM | Networking at the stairs About the Speaker Jada Powell is the Founder of Powell Consulting Group, where she works with industrial, energy, oil and gas, construction, and service-based companies to build stronger commercial infrastructure and more consistent business development momentum. Her work focuses on helping mid-market companies move beyond relationship-only growth into more intentional, visible, and scalable commercial strategies. This session is part of the Industrial Growth Series, a three-part in-person series at The Ion focused on how established industrial companies can remain visible, competitive, and positioned for the next stage of growth.

From Ion District

item.title: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas Showcase (Early)
item.description:
Monday, August 24, 2026 at 7 PM

Location: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas at Rio Hotel & Casino, 3700 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, NV, 89103, United States

This post contains affiliate links. We may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. Official Tickets Resale Tickets Comedy Cellar Las Vegas brings one of the most legendary names in stand-up comedy to the heart of Las Vegas. Located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino, this intimate comedy club is the West Coast home of New York City’s world-famous Comedy Cellar, the venue that helped launch the careers of comedy icons including Dave Chappelle, Chris Rock, Jon Stewart, Ray Romano, Amy Schumer, Aziz Ansari, and countless others. Unlike traditional comedy shows featuring a single headliner, Comedy Cellar presents a carefully curated lineup of professional comedians every night. Audiences can expect multiple performers during each show, featuring a mix of nationally touring headliners, television favorites, Comedy Central veterans, Netflix performers, and rising stars from around the world. No two shows are exactly alike, making every visit a unique experience. Surprise drop-in appearances from major comedians performing elsewhere in Las Vegas have become part of the club’s reputation, giving audiences the chance to see comedy superstars in an intimate setting. Event Details Venue: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas at Rio Hotel & Casino Location: 3700 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89103 Show Schedule: Nightly performances throughout the year Age Requirement: Recommended for audiences 18+ due to mature comedy content About the Venue Opened in 2018, Comedy Cellar Las Vegas was designed to recreate the atmosphere and energy of the original Greenwich Village club that has become one of the most respected comedy venues in the world. The 300-seat showroom offers excellent sightlines and an intimate setting that allows audiences to experience stand-up comedy exactly as it was meant to be seen: up close and personal. The venue combines the excitement of a Las Vegas night out with the authentic feel of a classic New York comedy club. Guests can enjoy a comfortable showroom environment while watching some of the best comedians working today perform in a setting that encourages spontaneity, crowd interaction, and unforgettable moments. Conveniently located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino just minutes from the Las Vegas Strip, the venue offers easy access for both tourists and local comedy fans. What to Expect Expect a fast-paced evening featuring multiple comedians performing throughout the show. The Comedy Cellar is known for showcasing a wide variety of comedic styles, from observational humor and storytelling to sharp social commentary, crowd work, and cutting-edge stand-up. Whether you’re discovering a future comedy star or watching a seasoned veteran perfect their craft, every show delivers the authentic comedy club experience that has made the Comedy Cellar one of the most respected brands in stand-up comedy. item.title: Inprint Andrea Bajani & Claire Vaye Watkins Reading
item.description:
Monday, August 24, 2026 at 7:30 PM

Location: Congregation Emanu El, 1500 Sunset Boulevard, Houston, TX, 77005

Season tickets are on sale here.   Andrea Bajani and Claire Vaye Watkins will read from their new novels The Anniversary (translated by Geoffrey Brock) and Yellow Pine, respectively, followed by an on-stage conversation led by professor and National Book Critics Circle Award finalist Lacy M. Johnson. The evening will conclude with a book sale and signing. The event is presented as part of the 2026/2027 Inprint Margarett Root Brown Reading Series.  Andrea Bajani is one of the most recognized and lauded authors of contemporary Italian and European literature. His many novels include If You Kept a Record of Sins, called “astonishing” by The New York Times, and Every Promise, which won the Bagutta Prize, the oldest Italian literary prize. A self-described existential writer, he often examines the personal, philosophical, and political, while confronting the unanswerable. A professor and international writer-in-residence at Rice University, Bajani joins us with his latest novel, The Anniversary, which won the 2025 Strega Prize, one of Europe’s major literary awards. Currently being translated into more than 25 languages, The Anniversary is a subtle yet heartrending portrait of an abusive marriage in patriarchal Italy and a son’s liberating decision to cut contact with his parents. The Times Literary Supplement writes, “Bajani’s prose is sharp and brims with psychological insights . . . Perhaps its most salient feature—in deft translation by Geoffrey Brock—is its skill at depicting alienation . . . Like Albert Camus, Bajani is a poet of estrangement.” Claire Vaye Watkins has been called “the most riveting voice of the unsalvageable West” (Los Angeles Times). Her debut novel Gold Fame Citrus, inspired by the Californian drought and by the lives of outcasts in the desert, blends climate fiction with environmental history. Born in Bishop, California and raised in the Mojave Desert on the Amargosa River, Watkins is also the author of the novel I Love You But I’ve Chosen Darkness and the short story collection Battleborn, winner of the Story Prize, the Dylan Thomas Prize, and the New York Public Library’s Young Lions Fiction Award. A National Book Foundation “5 Under 35” honoree and a Guggenheim Fellow, Watkins comes to Houston with her newest work Yellow Pine, described by author Megha Majumdar as “an exhilarating novel about a woman in the Mojave desert who wants to be a mother one more time, wants to love freely and arrange her life freely, wants to live outside the maze of money and ads and being sold to, a novel with huge and electric convictions.” Lacy M. Johnson is a Houston-based professor, curator, and activist, and is author of The Reckonings and The Other Side — both National Book Critics Circle Award finalists — and Trespasses. She is editor, with the designer Cheryl Beckett, of More City Than Water: A Houston Flood Atlas. She teaches creative nonfiction at Rice University, where she is the Director of the MFA in Creative Writing Program, and is also the Founding Director of the Houston Flood Museum.

Located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino, this intimate comedy club is the West Coast home of New York City’s world-famous Comedy Cellar, the venue that helped launch the careers of comedy icons including Dave Chappelle, Chris Rock, Jon Stewart, Ray Romano, Amy Schumer, Aziz Ansari, and countless others. Unlike traditional comedy shows featuring a single headliner, Comedy Cellar presents a carefully curated lineup of professional comedians every night. Audiences can expect multiple performers during each show, featuring a mix of nationally touring headliners, television favorites, Comedy Central veterans, Netflix performers, and rising stars from around the world. No two shows are exactly alike, making every visit a unique experience. Surprise drop-in appearances from major comedians performing elsewhere in Las Vegas have become part of the club’s reputation, giving audiences the chance to see comedy superstars in an intimate setting. Event Details Venue: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas at Rio Hotel & Casino Location: 3700 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89103 Show Schedule: Nightly performances throughout the year Age Requirement: Recommended for audiences 18+ due to mature comedy content About the Venue Opened in 2018, Comedy Cellar Las Vegas was designed to recreate the atmosphere and energy of the original Greenwich Village club that has become one of the most respected comedy venues in the world. The 300-seat showroom offers excellent sightlines and an intimate setting that allows audiences to experience stand-up comedy exactly as it was meant to be seen: up close and personal. The venue combines the excitement of a Las Vegas night out with the authentic feel of a classic New York comedy club. Guests can enjoy a comfortable showroom environment while watching some of the best comedians working today perform in a setting that encourages spontaneity, crowd interaction, and unforgettable moments. Conveniently located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino just minutes from the Las Vegas Strip, the venue offers easy access for both tourists and local comedy fans. item.title: Full Day Continuing Education
item.description:
Tuesday, August 25, 2026 at 9 AM

Location: Architecture Center Houston, 902 Commerce St., Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Urbanism Continuum CE day   9:00-9:30am Breakfast and Registration 9:30-10:45am / Presentation Building Bridges: Collaborative Placemaking in the Bayou City – 1.25 AIA HSW Presented by Michael Robinson, PLA, ASLA, Principal, SWA Group Michael is a landscape architect focused on the intersection of infrastructure and public space. He leads the design and implementation of complex park, trail, and civic landscape projects, connecting regional systems into cohesive, accessible environments. His work spans planning through realization, coordinating multidisciplinary teams and public agencies to deliver resilient, buildable solutions. With a background in both architecture and landscape architecture, he brings a systems-based approach that integrates environmental performance, mobility, and user experience into high-performing public landscapes. 11:00-12:00pm / Presentation  Universal Design: Building Accessible and Healthy Spaces – 1.00 AIA HSW (Barrier Free) Presented by Kyle J. Mutz, Director, University of Houston / Justin Dart Jr. Student Accessibility Center Kyle is the Director of the Justin Dart Jr. Student Accessibility Center at the University of Houston, where he champions accessibility, inclusion, and student success. Drawing from both his professional expertise and lived experience growing up with a disability, Kyle is committed to creating equitable opportunities for all. A former U.S. wheelchair racing athlete, he brings a unique perspective on disability advocacy and is dedicated to advancing the legacy of Justin Dart Jr. through education and empowerment.   12:00-12:30pm – Break for Lunch    12:30-1:45pm / Presentation  From Paint to Policy: How Tactical Urbanism Became a Capital Project – 1.25 AIA HSW & 1.25 LA/CES HSW Presented by Ed Pettitt, MPH – President of Columbia Tap and Urban Planner with Asakura Robinson Ed is an urban planner and One Health specialist whose academic path spans human biology at Cornell University, global health and healthcare management at the University of Texas School of Public Health, and doctoral studies in Urban Planning and Environmental Policy at Texas Southern University. In addition, Ed is also the President of the Columbia Tap Trail.  He provides organizational leadership by guiding the board, strengthening partnerships, advancing strategic initiatives, and overseeing programs that support equitable community development along the Columbia Tap Trail. 2:00-3:15pm / Presentation + Tour Reclaiming Main Street: Designing a Lasting Legacy in the Public Realm  – 1.25 AIA HSW & 1.25 LA/CES HSW Presented by Alex Ramirez, PLA & Sarah Smith, PLA, CDT, Design Workshop Alex is a Principal in the Houston studio at Design Workshop, with expertise as both a landscape architect and urban designer. His diverse experience spans across the private and public sectors, involving every phase of the design process—from conceptual planning and site analysis to construction documentation and detailed observation. Alex is dedicated to delivering top-tier work by crafting innovative design solutions for plazas, streetscapes, parks, and open spaces. His approach integrates social, cultural, economic, and environmental considerations, ensuring that each project enhances the surrounding neighborhoods and communities in meaningful ways. Sarah is a landscape architect in our Houston studio with a passion for the outdoors, thoughtful design, and creating meaningful places. From concept through construction, she brings creativity, attention to detail, and a collaborative approach to projects ranging from parks and corporate campuses to urban streetscapes. Sarah earned her Bachelor of Landscape Architecture from Louisiana State University and is an active member of ULI, Central Houston, and ASLA.   Continuing Education Credits: AIA = 4.75 HSW LA/CES = 3.75 HSW   Individual classes are not available for the event. Pre-registered pricing includes breakfast and lunch. Parking is not included. A minimum of 3 business days’ notice is required to receive a full refund if you need to cancel your reservation. Online registration will close Thursday, August 20 Onsite registration is available for day of (breakfast and lunch is NOT included)

item.title: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas Showcase (Early)
item.description:
Tuesday, August 25, 2026 at 7 PM

Location: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas at Rio Hotel & Casino, 3700 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, NV, 89103, United States

This post contains affiliate links. We may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. Official Tickets Resale Tickets Comedy Cellar Las Vegas brings one of the most legendary names in stand-up comedy to the heart of Las Vegas. Located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino, this intimate comedy club is the West Coast home of New York City’s world-famous Comedy Cellar, the venue that helped launch the careers of comedy icons including Dave Chappelle, Chris Rock, Jon Stewart, Ray Romano, Amy Schumer, Aziz Ansari, and countless others. Unlike traditional comedy shows featuring a single headliner, Comedy Cellar presents a carefully curated lineup of professional comedians every night. Audiences can expect multiple performers during each show, featuring a mix of nationally touring headliners, television favorites, Comedy Central veterans, Netflix performers, and rising stars from around the world. No two shows are exactly alike, making every visit a unique experience. Surprise drop-in appearances from major comedians performing elsewhere in Las Vegas have become part of the club’s reputation, giving audiences the chance to see comedy superstars in an intimate setting. Event Details Venue: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas at Rio Hotel & Casino Location: 3700 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89103 Show Schedule: Nightly performances throughout the year Age Requirement: Recommended for audiences 18+ due to mature comedy content About the Venue Opened in 2018, Comedy Cellar Las Vegas was designed to recreate the atmosphere and energy of the original Greenwich Village club that has become one of the most respected comedy venues in the world. The 300-seat showroom offers excellent sightlines and an intimate setting that allows audiences to experience stand-up comedy exactly as it was meant to be seen: up close and personal. The venue combines the excitement of a Las Vegas night out with the authentic feel of a classic New York comedy club. Guests can enjoy a comfortable showroom environment while watching some of the best comedians working today perform in a setting that encourages spontaneity, crowd interaction, and unforgettable moments. Conveniently located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino just minutes from the Las Vegas Strip, the venue offers easy access for both tourists and local comedy fans. What to Expect Expect a fast-paced evening featuring multiple comedians performing throughout the show. The Comedy Cellar is known for showcasing a wide variety of comedic styles, from observational humor and storytelling to sharp social commentary, crowd work, and cutting-edge stand-up. Whether you’re discovering a future comedy star or watching a seasoned veteran perfect their craft, every show delivers the authentic comedy club experience that has made the Comedy Cellar one of the most respected brands in stand-up comedy. For comedy fans visiting Las Vegas, Comedy Cellar is widely considered one of the best places in the city to experience live stand-up comedy any night of the week.

item.title: EnLAce: Domino Night with LiA Maestros
item.description:
Wednesday, August 26, 2026 at 6 PM

Location: Architecture Center Houston, 902 Commerce St., Houston, TX, 77002, United States

This year’s Enlace introduces a new and engaging format: a rotating domino game night designed to spark genuine conversations and connections in a relaxed, interactive environment. Through time-based gameplay and table rotations, participants will have the opportunity to engage with several LiA Maestros throughout the evening, creating a unique, fun, and memorable mentoring experience. EnLAce is open to all professionals looking for career development and growth. No dominoes experience required. We will begin the evening with a brief tutorial to make it easy and enjoyable for everyone to participate. Luis Ayala, AIA, Luis Ayala Studio Sofia Fonseca de Nino, AIA Michael Gonzales, AIA, protolab Yvette Herrera Duran, Assoc. AIA, Stantec Daniel Ortiz, AIA, RDLR Bayardo Selva, AIA, Cre8 Cindy Villareal, AIA, O’Connell Robertson Generously sponsored by Perkins&Will.  Luis Ayala, AIA, Owner, Luis Ayala Studio Luis is a Paraguayan architect that migrated to Houston in 2007. He has focused mostly on the design of education facilities for higher education institutions and K-12 schools. His expertise includes campus design, master planning, programming, and facility design. Luis has many other skills that complement his abilities as a designer and architect. Sustainability is one of Luis’s stronger interests, and many of his projects have received design awards recognizing his innovation in green design. Luis is also an avid architectural photographer, recognized in 2017 by the Texas Society of Architects with the Award for Excellence in the Promotion of Architecture Trough the Media. Luis fluently speaks Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, and English. In 2016, Luis was distinguished by YAF Houston as a part Emerging Voices Exhibition and later the same year by AIA National as an Emerging Professional. Recently, in 2020 the AIA Houston awarded him with the Ben Brewer Award for Young Architects. Michael Gonzales, AIA, Owner, protolab Michael Gonzales is the owner and principal of Protolab Architects. Michael specializes in digital fabrication innovation for civic, cultural and commercial projects. He has extensive experience working with the latest fabrication technologies to develop efficient strategies for optimal construction and project delivery at all scales and complexities. Michael is also an Instructional Associate Professor at the University of Houston Gerald D. Hines College of Architecture and Design where he focuses on the integration of digital design and fabrication. He actively publishes and lectures on emerging techniques in computation and design   Yvette Herrera Duran, Assoc. AIA, Stantec Yvette Herrera Duran is an architectural designer based in Houston Texas. Her experience expands from many years in high-end residential design to now corporate commercial architecture at Page. Born and raised in Guatemala, she moved to Miami to pursue her Undergraduate Studies in Interior Design at Florida International University. After working for a few years at a high-end residential architecture firm, where architecture and interiors were strongly interconnected, she pursued her master’s in architecture at Rice University. From an early age she was trained in flamenco dancing, which she has continued practicing. During her years in Miami, she trained in ballroom dance and later, while getting her masters, she complimented her knowledge in the arts with theatre classes.  All these various art languages influence how she experiences spaces and the development of her detailed oriented designs.  She currently works in various design typologies from academic to healthcare to multifamily communities. Daniel Ortiz, AIA, President and Managing Principal, RDLR Architects Daniel Ortiz, AIA, was born in Ecuador and serves as President and Managing Principal of RDLR Architects, a Houston firm dedicated to community-driven design. Under his leadership, RDLR creates architecture that strengthens neighborhoods through public, nonprofit, transit, education, and housing projects. He also serves as Board President of Avenue CDC and Chairman of TIRZ 21, advancing equitable community development in Houston’s Near Northside. Bayardo Selva, AIA, Cre8 Bayardo has turn his childhood building blocks play time into an Architectural career that expands over 20 years. His experienced has allowed him to engage a wide variety of project types and scales. He actively participates in the community through different organizations promoting architecture, protecting the environment, mentoring the youth and celebrating diversity including AIA Houston Young Architects Forum (Chair, 2014), AIA Board of Directors 2015-2018 and 2023-present (AIAH Board President, 2026), Houston Hispanic Architects and Engineers Board Member 2016-2019, Houston MOD Board Member 2019-Present, Houston Fit Running Club 2012-Present, and founding member of the AIA Houston Latinos in Architecture. He considers himself a student of the profession and enjoys perfecting his craft! Cindy Villareal, AIA, Houston Office Director, O’Connell Robertson Cindy Villarreal is a seasoned leader in architectural planning and project acquisition, with a strong focus on higher education and healthcare initiatives across Texas. As the Houston Office Director, Cindy is instrumental in expanding business development efforts throughout the Houston region while driving strategic growth statewide. With decades of experience in the design of higher education and Science and Technology facilities, Cindy has led projects ranging from allied health and nursing schools to dental institutions and advanced diagnostics and neuroscience laboratories. Her expertise lies in managing multidisciplinary design teams and fostering collaboration to ensure projects are delivered successfully. Cindy is a passionate advocate for sustainable and resilient design. She champions human-centric environments that prioritize occupant well-being and support thriving communities. Her leadership continues to shape spaces that are not only functional and efficient but also inspiring and inclusive.

From AIA Houston

item.title: Dave Landau LIVE at Blue Note Hawaii
item.description:
Wednesday, August 26, 2026 at 6:30 PM

Location: Blue Note Hawaii, 2335 Kalakaua Avenue, Honolulu, HI, 96815, United States

Official TicketsResale Tickets This post contains affiliate links. We may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. About the Performer Dave Landau is one of the most sought-after stand-up comedians working today. Getting his start in Detroit at the Second City’s Conservatory, Dave developed a fast-paced, sharp style with a strong improv background that sets him apart from the crowd. His laid-back demeanor and dark style of comedy landed him on Comedy Central’s This is Not Happening (3.1 million views) and as a Season 8 finalist on NBC’s Last Comic Standing. He is the creator of Normal World, currently on BlazeTV, and his impressive resume includes The Artie Lange and Anthony Cumia Show, The Anthony Cumia Show with Dave Landau, and Louder with Crowder. Dave has also appeared on the Joe Rogan Experience, Kill Tony, Fox Across America, Gutfeld!, and Fox Saturday Night. He regularly performs at clubs and theaters across the country and has opened for legends like Dave Chappelle, Dennis Miller, and Steven Wright. Event Details Date: Wednesday, August 26, 2026 Time: 6:30 PM HST (Doors open at 5:00 PM) Venue: Blue Note Hawaii, 2335 Kalakaua Avenue, Honolulu, HI 96815 Show Duration: Approximately 75-90 minutes Age Restrictions: 18+ event Note: A second show is also available at 9:00 PM the same evening About the Venue Blue Note Hawaii is Honolulu’s premier intimate live entertainment venue, located at 2335 Kalakaua Avenue in the heart of Waikiki. Part of the legendary Blue Note Jazz Club brand, this venue brings world-class comedy and music to the islands in an intimate, club-style setting. The venue features communal and premium seating with a first-come, first-served policy — so arriving early is highly recommended to secure the best seats. A full dinner menu and full bar are available throughout the show, with a $20 food or beverage minimum per person required. Blue Note Hawaii has a capacity of approximately 300 guests, creating an incredibly intimate atmosphere where you feel close to the performer. The Waikiki location means you’re steps away from the beach, world-class restaurants, and the vibrant nightlife of one of the world’s most famous resort destinations. What to Expect Dave Landau’s show at Blue Note Hawaii is part of the venue’s acclaimed Blue Note Comedy Series. This is an intimate stand-up performance in a dinner-club setting — a very different experience from a large arena show. Expect sharp, fast-paced comedy with a dark edge, delivered in an up-close-and-personal environment. Dave’s improv background means no two shows are exactly alike — he feeds off the crowd and the energy of the room. Arrive at 5:00 PM when doors open to enjoy dinner before the show and secure your preferred seating. This is the early show (6:30 PM). A late show is also available at 9:00 PM for those who prefer a later start. Both shows are 18+ only, so please bring valid photo ID. Ticket Information Price Range: $25 – $35 (plus fees; resale prices may vary) Premium Seating: $35 (+$10.90 fees) Loge Seating & Bar Area: $25 (+$9.10 fees) $20 food or beverage minimum per person required at the venue Purchase official tickets through TicketWeb (Ticketmaster partner), or find resale tickets through VividSeats. item.title: Heights Garden Club Presents: Angel Wing Arts brings this Bee Watering Station Craft to the Heights Garden Club
item.description:
Wednesday, August 26, 2026 at 6:30 PM

Location: Houston Heights City Hall & Fire Station, 107 W. 12th Street, Houston, TX, 77008, United States

AUGUST 26th at 6:30pm, join us at the Heights Fire Station Carolyn, of Angel Wing Arts, (Instagram @cacoatesart or @anglewingarts) and one of our own, will lead this workshop. Carolyn has been active in the arts for over 30 years, from faux finishes to murals to art pieces. She has worked with clients and their art needs, and her work itself is whimsical and fun. Please join us on August 26, at our favorite spot to mingle, the historic Heights Fire station on 12th and Yale streets. There will be a demo, and plenty of inspiration to kick off your creativity!! Each participant will construct two bee watering stations from clay pots and saucers and then decorate them with paints and pens, as seen in the photo. Let’s help our bees and butterflies in this heat by providing them a safe place to get a drink that YOU are providing with your cute, personalized vessel. Reserve your spot through Sign-Up Genius so we have an accurate headcount and can make sure we have the right amount of supplies on hand. But hurry, there is only room for 25 guests and the deadline to sign up is August 19th. $20 cash per person, ages 12 and up, to be paid at the door. Please, no unaccompanied minors. Doors opens at 6:30pm, Class is 7-9pm. Please arrive early so that instruction can begin on time. Water and some light refreshments will be provided, but please consider bringing a snack to share, if you are so inclined. You may bring your own adult beverages if you wish.

Official Tickets Resale Tickets Comedy Cellar Las Vegas brings one of the most legendary names in stand-up comedy to the heart of Las Vegas. Located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino, this intimate comedy club is the West Coast home of New York City’s world-famous Comedy Cellar, the venue that helped launch the careers of comedy icons including Dave Chappelle, Chris Rock, Jon Stewart, Ray Romano, Amy Schumer, Aziz Ansari, and countless others. Unlike traditional comedy shows featuring a single headliner, Comedy Cellar presents a carefully curated lineup of professional comedians every night. Audiences can expect multiple performers during each show, featuring a mix of nationally touring headliners, television favorites, Comedy Central veterans, Netflix performers, and rising stars from around the world. No two shows are exactly alike, making every visit a unique experience. Surprise drop-in appearances from major comedians performing elsewhere in Las Vegas have become part of the club’s reputation, giving audiences the chance to see comedy superstars in an intimate setting. Event Details Venue: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas at Rio Hotel & Casino Location: 3700 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89103 Show Schedule: Nightly performances throughout the year Age Requirement: Recommended for audiences 18+ due to mature comedy content About the Venue Opened in 2018, Comedy Cellar Las Vegas was designed to recreate the atmosphere and energy of the original Greenwich Village club that has become one of the most respected comedy venues in the world. The 300-seat showroom offers excellent sightlines and an intimate setting that allows audiences to experience stand-up comedy exactly as it was meant to be seen: up close and personal. The venue combines the excitement of a Las Vegas night out with the authentic feel of a classic New York comedy club. Guests can enjoy a comfortable showroom environment while watching some of the best comedians working today perform in a setting that encourages spontaneity, crowd interaction, and unforgettable moments. Conveniently located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino just minutes from the Las Vegas Strip, the venue offers easy access for both tourists and local comedy fans. What to Expect Expect a fast-paced evening featuring multiple comedians performing throughout the show. The Comedy Cellar is known for showcasing a wide variety of comedic styles, from observational humor and storytelling to sharp social commentary, crowd work, and cutting-edge stand-up. Whether you’re discovering a future comedy star or watching a seasoned veteran perfect their craft, every show delivers the authentic comedy club experience that has made the Comedy Cellar one of the most respected brands in stand-up comedy. For comedy fans visiting Las Vegas, Comedy Cellar is widely considered one of the best places in the city to experience live stand-up comedy any night of the week.

item.title: NASA Tech Talks: Rice University’s Space Humanities Initiative
item.description:
Thursday, August 27, 2026 at 6 PM

Location: Ion, 4201 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

We want HOU! Join us to discover NASA’s toughest tech challenges—and apply your skills and expertise to solve them. This month, NASA Tech Talks will feature Rice’s new Space Humanities Initiative, co-led by Alexander Regier, the William Faulkner Professor of English and chair of the Department of English and Creative Writing, and David Alexander, director of the Rice Space Institute and professor of physics and astronomy. Long before rockets, satellites or space stations, humans were already in a relationship with outer space. People looked up and named constellations. They told stories about the moon. They wrote poems, mapped stars and built myths around lights in the sky they could not touch. Across cultures and centuries, outer space functioned as more than a scientific mystery; it was a mirror for human longing, fear, imagination and hope. The Rice Space Initiative brings scholars across disciplines together to examine how culture, language, ethics and imagination shape space exploration, and how space exploration shapes them in return.  Please join us for a discussion of how the Initiative came to be, and how it might provide a sustained space where questions about ownership, settlement, commercial use and planetary responsibility can be addressed in an interdisciplinary manner. Please join us after the talk for drinks and networking at Second Draught!   About the Speakers Dr. David Alexander is an astrophysics professor at Rice University and a faculty scholar at the Baker Institute for Public Policy. He also serves as the Director of the Rice Space Institute. Alexander was awarded an OBE by her majesty Queen Elizabeth in 2018 for services to the space industry and was named a Chevalier of the National Order of Merit by the French Republic in 2026.  He received a Presidential Early Career Award in 2004 and was appointed a Kavli Frontiers Fellow by the National Academy of Sciences in 2006. Alexander has served on many professional committees including the NASA Advisory Council’s Heliophysics Subcommittee, and the NASA Solar Heliospheric Management and Operations Working Group.  He was named a GlobalScot by the Scottish government and served as an elected member of the Board of Directors of the American Astronautical Society from 2018-2022. He served as Chair of the Aerospace Industry Committee of the Greater Houston Partnership, been on the Board of the Houston Spaceport Development Corporation since 2021 and was recently appointed to the Texas Aerospace Research and Space Economy Consortium Executive Committee.  Alexander received his Bachelor’s degree and doctorate from the University of Glasgow. Alexander Regier is the William Faulkner Professor of English in the Department of English and Creative Writing. He also holds a full appointment in the Department of Modern and Classical Languages, Literatures and Cultures. Regier is the author and editor of multiple books and articles on literature, art, and culture. His publications cover a range of subjects, from eighteenth-century philosophy and Romantic literature to outer space, awkwardness, fragmentation, ruins, and sports. In recent years, Regier has received an Alexander von Humboldt Fellowship for Experienced Researchers, as well as Fellowships at the National Humanities Center, the Center for Research in the Arts, Social Sciences, and Humanities at the University of Cambridge, and a Visiting Fellowship at the University of Exeter. He has also won multiple awards, amongst others, from the National Endowment for the Humanities. From 2023 to 2026, he was chair of the Department of English and Creative Writing at Rice and is now co-director of the Space Humanities Initiative. Dario Robleto is an artist, writer, and filmmaker based in Houston, Texas. His work has been exhibited widely and is held in prominent collections, including the Harvard Art Museum, the Whitney Museum of American Art, and the National Gallery of Art in Washington, D.C. He has held research fellowships and residencies at institutions including the Smithsonian Museum of American History, the SETI Institute, and the Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University. From 2018 to 2023, he served as Artist-at-Large at Northwestern University’s McCormick School of Engineering and the Block Museum of Art. In 2020, he served as a research consultant for the popular science television series Cosmos: Possible Worlds. In 2016, Robleto was appointed Texas State 3-D Visual Artist, and in 2025, he was awarded an Honorary Doctorate of Humane Letters from Middlebury College. He is currently working on his first book, The Heartbeat at the Edge of the Solar System: Science, Emotion, and the Golden Record, co-authored with Harvard art historian Jennifer Roberts. It will be published by Scribner in 2027. Ryn Delpapa is a change-maker who believes in impact. A neuroarts tech founder, interdisciplinary artist, and speaker on a mission, they honor life’s biodiversity, from plants to people. Ryn is a recent 2026 TEDxHouston Countdown speaker, 2025 4.0 Tiny Fellow, and CXC Changemakers for the Planet Fellow, bridging creativity, health, and environmental stewardship within their venture, AR+E COMETS, a global health studio. As a 2024 City of Houston City Initiative grant awardee, their Art for Climate Resilience community arts-in-health program shaped community health in Houston’s Third and Fifth Wards. With a B.S. in International Nutrition from the University of Texas at Austin and a kaleidoscope career from Houston to Chengdu, China, their global health background, 8 years in B2B SaaS tech, and arts-in-health research enable them to bridge creativity and planetary health. Work they share through their venture, consultancy, and Earthly Bonds podcast, where they explore health, from brain to biosphere, for creative, resilient living. Montgomery B. Goforth has more than 40 years of experience as both Engineer and Manager in a variety of highly technical space and defense-related efforts.  After working for a small defense contractor specializing in anti-submarine warfare, he joined NASA’s Johnson Space Center in 1990.  He has held leadership positions in multiple JSC Directorates and Program Offices. In his previous role as Assistant Director of the JSC Engineering Directorate, he established a framework to better focus Engineering’s efforts towards Human Spaceflight technology and systems development consistent with JSC and Agency goals for exploration. Mr. Goforth is now serving as Acting Director of the Business Development & Technology Integration Office at JSC, and as the JSC Chief Technologist.  In these capacities he will be helping to expand the Houston Aerospace Community through the identification of opportunities to develop space/terrestrial technologies of interest to JSC and Human Space Exploration.  Mr. Goforth was born in East Texas, raised in Southern California and Arizona, and graduated from Rice University (BSME 1982, MSME 1987). About NASA Tech Talks In these presentations, occurring the fourth Thursdays of the month, Mr. Montgomery Goforth and other aerospace subject matter experts will discuss the technology development challenges faced by NASA’s Johnson Space Center and the surrounding Aerospace community in our ongoing efforts as the hub of human spaceflight. Presentations will focus on the ways in which these challenges, and the associated opportunities, can be leveraged by Houston’s innovation community. We will continue to identify potential space/terrestrial technologies of interest to Human Spaceflight.  Past NASA Tech Talks have included topics such as: From Space to Startup: Leveraging NASA Technology and Innovation to Propel Your Growing Enterprise Disruptive Filter Technology for Spacecraft Water Treatment:  The New Promise of Graphene Lunar dust capture using novel multiplexed inertial filter Lunar Passive Fuel Cell Technologies: Microbes in Space

item.title: Author Talk with Dr. Pamela Toler, Author of The Dragon From Chicago
item.description:
Thursday, August 27, 2026 at 6:30 PM

Location: Albert and Ethel Herzstein Theater on the Mady and Ken Kades Stage

Join Holocaust Museum Houston for a night with Dr. Pamela Toler, Author of The Dragon from Chicago: The Untold Story of an American Reporter in Nazi Germany.      “Today we face an alarming upsurge in the spread of misinformation and attempts by powerful figures to discredit facts so they can seize control of our political and cultural narratives. These are threats American journalist Sigrid Schultz knew all too well. The Chicago Tribune’s Berlin bureau chief and primary foreign correspondent for Central Europe from 1925 to January 1941, Schultz witnessed Hitler’s rise to power and was one of the first reporters—male or female—to warn American readers of the growing dangers of Nazism.  She was one of the last to leave Berlin before it was too late.     In The Dragon From Chicago, historian Pamela Toler tells the story of Schultz’s years spent courageously reporting the news from Berlin, from the revolts of 1919 through the Nazi rise to power and Allied air raids over Berlin in 1941. At a time when women reporters rarely wrote front-page stories, Schultz regularly  reported the truth about Nazi Germany in the face of censorship and the threat of expulsion, internment, or death. The Nazis called Schultz “that dragon from Chicago.” One of her fellow correspondents called her “Adolph Hitler’s greatest enemy.” Schultz herself claimed to be “just a reporter.” Her story is a powerful account of one woman standing up for truth in an era marked by the spread of disinformation and propaganda spawned by hate.”     Books will be available for purchase by credit card.

The 300-seat showroom offers excellent sightlines and an intimate setting that allows audiences to experience stand-up comedy exactly as it was meant to be seen: up close and personal. The venue combines the excitement of a Las Vegas night out with the authentic feel of a classic New York comedy club. Guests can enjoy a comfortable showroom environment while watching some of the best comedians working today perform in a setting that encourages spontaneity, crowd interaction, and unforgettable moments. Conveniently located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino just minutes from the Las Vegas Strip, the venue offers easy access for both tourists and local comedy fans. What to Expect Expect a fast-paced evening featuring multiple comedians performing throughout the show. The Comedy Cellar is known for showcasing a wide variety of comedic styles, from observational humor and storytelling to sharp social commentary, crowd work, and cutting-edge stand-up. Whether you’re discovering a future comedy star or watching a seasoned veteran perfect their craft, every show delivers the authentic comedy club experience that has made the Comedy Cellar one of the most respected brands in stand-up comedy. For comedy fans visiting Las Vegas, Comedy Cellar is widely considered one of the best places in the city to experience live stand-up comedy any night of the week.

About the Performer Roy Wood Jr. is one of the most versatile and celebrated comedians working today. An Emmy-nominated comedian, documentary producer, WGA-nominated writer, actor, and radio personality, Wood Jr. is best known for his eight years as a correspondent on Comedy Central’s Emmy-winning The Daily Show (2015–2023). In 2023, he guest hosted The Daily Show and headlined the White House Correspondents’ Dinner to its highest ratings since 2017. His fourth stand-up special, Lonely Flowers, premiered on Hulu on January 17, 2025, earning widespread critical acclaim. He is also the host of CNN’s Have I Got News for You, an American adaptation of the long-running UK comedy series. Wood Jr. recently released his debut memoir The Man of Many Fathers with Crown Publishing (October 2025) and will appear alongside Keanu Reeves and Jonah Hill in the upcoming comedy film Outcome. Forbes has called him “One of comedy’s best journalists,” and Variety named him “One of 10 Comics to Watch.” Event Details Date: Friday, August 28, 2026 Show Time: 6:30 PM HST (Doors open at 5:00 PM) Venue: Blue Note Hawaii, 2335 Kalakaua Avenue, Honolulu, HI 96815 Age Restriction: 18+ Event — Valid photo ID required at entry Content Warning: Adult language and mature themes About the Venue Blue Note Hawaii is Honolulu’s most celebrated intimate live entertainment venue, located at 2335 Kalakaua Avenue in the heart of Waikiki. As part of the iconic Blue Note Jazz Club brand, this venue has hosted some of the world’s greatest performers in an atmosphere that blends tropical island charm with sophisticated nightlife. The venue offers communal seating on a first come, first served basis — arriving early is strongly recommended to secure the best seats. A full bar and complete dinner menu are available throughout the show, with a $20 food or beverage minimum per person. The intimate layout ensures excellent sightlines from virtually every seat in the house. Blue Note Hawaii’s warm, inviting atmosphere makes it the perfect setting for an evening of world-class comedy. Parking is available throughout the Waikiki area, with multiple nearby garages and street parking options within easy walking distance. What to Expect This early Friday evening show features Roy Wood Jr. performing his signature brand of sharp, socially observant stand-up comedy. Known for his charismatic delivery and thought-provoking material, Wood Jr. blends current events, personal storytelling, and razor-sharp wit into a seamless and unforgettable performance. Audiences can expect a polished, high-energy set from one of comedy’s most respected voices. Wood Jr.’s material is both hilarious and insightful — the kind of comedy that makes you laugh and think at the same time. This is a rare opportunity to see a major comedy headliner in an intimate club setting in Hawaii. Doors open at 5:00 PM, giving you plenty of time to settle in, enjoy a full dinner from the menu, and grab drinks before the show begins. Seating is communal and first come, first served — arrive early for the best spots. This is an 18+ event — please bring valid photo ID. About the Performer Francisco Ramos is a bilingual stand-up comedian who has been making audiences laugh across the United States with his unique blend of English and Spanish comedy. Known for his high-energy performances and sharp cultural observations, Ramos has built a devoted following among Latino audiences and comedy fans of all backgrounds. His comedy draws from his experiences growing up in a Latino household, navigating two cultures, and the universal absurdities of family life. item.title: Classic Albums Live: Led Zeppelin IV at Miller Outdoor Theatre
item.description:
Friday, August 28, 2026 at 8 PM

Location: Miller Outdoor Theatre, 6000 Hermann Park Dr, Houston, TX, 77030, United States

Miller Outdoor Theatre welcomes Classic Albums Live back to the Hermann Park stage for a live concert recreating Led Zeppelin IV—an incredible album featuring some of Led Zeppelin’s most beloved and recognizable recordings—note for note and cut for cut under the stars. Audiences can sing along with favorites like as “Rock and Roll”, “When the Levee Breaks”, and of course, “Stairway to Heaven”. Considered one of the greatest albums of all time, Led Zeppelin IV is an album full of experimentation from the way it was recorded to the variety of arrangements. As the best-selling album of one of the best-selling bands, it sold 37 million+ copies worldwide. This performance was originally scheduled to showcase The Eagles’ Hotel California. Finding Your Seat at Miller Outdoor Theatre As always, all seats at Miller are free, but covered seating for popular evening shows usually requires a free assigned ticket reserved 24 hours in advance. Where: Stude Park – 1031 Stude Street, Houston, TX 77007 When: Usually every Saturday of the month, 8:00–10:00 AM. Check our events calendar for exact dates. Want to make an even bigger impact? Volunteers are needed to help guide riders, assist with equipment, and keep the event running smoothly. Whether you’re an experienced cyclist or just eager to lend a hand, your support helps ensure a safe, fun, and welcoming experience for all participants. May 31: Rocks and Minerals Explore the fascinating characteristics of the most important building blocks of Earth’s crust. July 26: Energy Exciting demonstrations explore the remarkable forms of energy we encounter every day. August 30: Dinosaur Discovery Peek into the thrilling daily life of the dinosaur: investigate what dinosaurs ate, how they hunted, and the adaptations they developed to survive in a harsh prehistoric world. September 27: Birds Encounter an amazing variety of birds and discover their fascinating ancestral roots, while learning about their adaptations for success. October 25: Ancient Egypt From mummies to the pyramids, experience amazing architectural and cultural aspects of Ancient Egypt. November 29: Little Bodies, Big Jobs! Brings a selection of live arthropods from the Cockrell Butterfly Center to your classroom. Audiences of all ages will have a unique opportunity to meet some of the hardest workers in the invertebrate world up close and personal. December 13:  Astronomy  Investigate our place in space and ways we study this exciting place full of planets, moons, stars, and galaxies.

From Levy Park Houston

item.title: First Fridays Presents John Milkereit
item.description:
Friday, September 4, 2026 at 7:30 PM

Location: Inprint House, 1520 W Main St, Houston, TX, 77006, United States

Free and open to the public Doors @ 7 pm Reading @ 7:30 pm Followed by an Open mic Inprint is proud to serve as the host for the First Fridays Reading Series. The First Fridays Reading Series is the oldest poetry series in Houston and was organized by Robert Clark from 1975-2019. Today, First Fridays events are curated and hosted by local community members. The September featured reader will be John Milkereit. John lives in Houston, Texas working as a mechanical engineer. His poetry journey did not begin well after being forced to read “Beowulf” in 6th grade. Several decades later, he found himself enjoying a poetry seminar at his local church on the poetry of Billy Collins, and then he took his first poetry class at Inprint in 2005. Later, he went on to complete an MFA in Creative Writing at the Rainier Writing Workshop. His poems have since appeared in various literary journals such as The Comstock Review, San Pedro River Review, and Naugatuck River Review. In December, Kelsay Books released his fifth collection of poems entitled, The Beginning of Undoing. For more information about the First Fridays Reading Series, click here. To join the First Fridays Facebook group, click here.

item.title: Edible Wild Plants
item.description:
Sunday, September 6, 2026 at 1 PM

$100 member / $125 nonmember (per person)Ages 16+, minors must be accompanied by an adult For most of human existence, the wilds supplied all our food and medicine. Join Dr. Mark “Merriwether” Vorderbruggen as he teaches you what your ancestors knew. This plant walkabout will give you hands-on (as well as nose, fingers, and taste bud) guidance on how to properly identify and utilize the wonderful wild plants of the Houston/East Texas region. Please dress for the weather and wear walking shoes. register online Instructor bio: Dr. Mark Vorderbruggen brings his background as a Ph.D. in chemistry to the world of Houston’s edible and medicinal wild plants. He is the author of “The Idiot’s Guide: Foraging,” runs the informative “Foraging Texas” website, formulates medicinal plant remedies through Medicine Man Plant Co., and is always educating about useful plants on TV, online, and in person.

item.title: Discover Nature Together Scavenger Hunts
item.description:
Sunday, September 6, 2026 at 2 PM

Free, donations appreciatedAll ages, minors must be accompanied by an adult Bring the whole family to the Houston Arboretum for free, themed scavenger hunts! Each month features a themed self-guided scavenger hunt where families can join us at our Nature Center before heading out to the trails to sharpen their observation skills and learn something new about nature. From spiders to fall foliage, every adventure is different! Please come prepared for the outdoors (closed toe shoes recommended, bring a water bottle, bug spray, etc).  Signs of LifeSeptember 6 We may not always see animals out and about, so how do we know they are here? They leave traces of themselves behind! From scat, to tracks, learn how to find the signs of life here at the Arboretum. Amazing ArachnidsOctober 10 Spiders are so much more than Halloween decorations. They fill the role of pest control specialist in our ecosystem. Want to learn more about these amazing arachnids? Then get into the Halloween spirit by learning more about spiders. Fall FoliageNovember 7 Although Houston is not known for its fall colors, there are still lots to learn about leaves! From deciduous to evergreen, here at the Arboretum we see leaves on the ground as well as in the trees all winter long. Join us and learn more about the difference between the two and why leaves are important in the fall. Animal HomesDecember 5 There is no central heating outdoors, so where do the animals go when they get cold? To their homes, of course! Burrows, leaves, nests, and so much more. Find out all the different types of animal homes and who lives in what.

From Houston Arboretum & Nature Center

item.title: Hatchlings
item.description:
Wednesday, September 9, 2026 at 10 AM

For children 0 – 18 months and their caregivers Babies in nature? Babies ARE nature! Babies who spend time outside are stronger, healthier, more confident, and better sleepers. Learn how to support your Hatchlings as they develop motor skills, test physical limits, cultivate their sense of wonder, and get messy in a safe place to try new things. Hatchlings will engage in outdoor nature play in this unique opportunity to interact, explore, and bond with their caregivers in the natural world. This program will be held outdoors and will include loose parts and messy play with natural sensory elements such as sand, mud, grass, sticks, leaves, and water. Space is limited and pre-registration is required for all Hatchlings classes. Select Wednesdays from 10:00 am – 11:00 am. Arboretum Member registration for Fall 2026 classes opens Tuesday, August 4 and Nonmember registration opens Tuesday, August 11. Become a Family Tree Member or above to access early registration and receive the Member rate. Pricing $12 member / $15 nonmember Per child/caregiver pair, per classMore than one caregiver may accompany a registered child. Minors must be accompanied by an adult. Upcoming Classes September september 9 september 16 september 23 November november 4 november 11 november 18 Additional Information Hatchlings classes are best for infants and toddlers who are creepers, crawlers, or new walkers up to 18 months old (not for older siblings), but even newborns benefit from sensory outdoor experiences Hatchlings will be held outdoors in rain or shine. Please dress yourself and your Hatchling for the weather and bring a spare change of clothes for your Hatchling. Hatchlings classes are for children 0-18 months and their caregivers only. Please do not bring older siblings to class. Accessibility This program is open to all abilities. Some areas where classes might be held are not stroller-friendly or wheelchair accessible. Please plan to carry your Hatchling to various locations and let us know if you need assistance with caregiver accessibility.

From Houston Arboretum & Nature Center

item.title: Braille Club
item.description:
Wednesday, September 9, 2026 at 12 PM

Location: The Lighthouse of Houston, 3602 West Dallas, Houston, TX, 77019, United States

The Lighthouse will be hosting a weekly Braille Club to help people learn functional Braille skills in a friendly group setting. The club meets every Wednesday from 12:00 PM to 2:00 PM. We will use fun games and activities to help everyone gain useful skills for daily life. Members will learn how to read playing cards for games, label items around their homes, and read signs and elevator buttons in public places. To join the club, participants need access to email and a notebook to keep their handout papers organized. Because the group learns new things every week, it is highly recommended to attend each session so you do not miss out on any important tips. REGISTER HERE.

item.title: September 11 – October 10, 2026 Exhibitions
item.description:
Friday, September 11, 2026 at 6 PM

Location: Box 13 ArtSpace, 6700 Harrisburg Blvd., Houston, TX, 77011, United States

BOX 13 ArtSpace is pleased to present four new exhibitions opening Friday, September 11 , 2026 6–9 PM. BOX 13 ArtSpace is pleased to present in the Front BOX gallery: “Cryptic Bodies,” an exhibition of four interdisciplinary Houston-based femme artists who work in sculpture, collage, zines, and socially engaged practices. As one excavates their layered work, bodies are revealed, both human, non-human, touching upon women’s health, fragmentary memories, and interconnected ecosystems and identities. The exhibit in the Back gallery features Chris Ireland’s “Dead Letter Office,” which explores home, memory, and placelessness through carefully constructed collages that combine fragments from lived experience, online archives, real estate listings, and personal photographs. For “Mother Earth Weaves Infinite” in the Box 13 Window BOX Gallery, Cathie Kayser and Ellen H Ray use a variety of materials and techniques, including fabrics, mulberry silks, soft sculpture, paper mache, and wire and paper sculptures to present an immersive experience that highlights the complexity of the mycorrhizal network. With this work, the artists invite viewers to consider the interconnectedness of all living systems. The Earth, and the universe encompassing it, is a master plan of intelligent design that holds lessons for us about systems that work. Moving to our Upstairs BOX gallery we are excited to introduce “Grip Strength: An Army of Lovers Shall Not Fail” by KT Abadir-Mullally. Through interactive soft sculptures and ceramics inspired by strength sports and queer activism, the exhibition invites visitors to engage with themes of queer resilience, desire, collective power, and resistance. The exhibitions continue through October 10, 2026. An Opening Reception will be held on Friday, September 11, 2026, 6–9 PM at BOX 13 ArtSpace, 6700 Harrisburg, Houston, TX 77011. This event is funded in part by the City of Houston through the Houston Arts Alliance and Houston MOCA. Additional support is provided by The Brown Foundation, Saint Arnold Brewing Company, Giant Texas Distillers, JP Morgan – Nancy O’Connor Fund, and all who help make our programming possible.

From East End Farmers Market

item.title: Cooking and Baking Class – September 2026
item.description:
Saturday, September 12, 2026 at 10 AM

Location: The Lighthouse of Houston, 3602 West Dallas, Houston, TX, 77019, United States

Cook. Learn. Belong. Step into the kitchen and discover the joy of cooking together. This free, hands-on monthly class invites youth ages 5–22 who are blind or low vision—and their families—to build essential kitchen skills in a welcoming, confidence-building space. Led by our O&M/ADL Specialist, Ruby Cabral, each session blends practical instruction with real-world techniques, empowering participants to move safely, independently, and creatively in the kitchen. item.title: September 11 – October 10, 2026 Exhibitions
item.description:
Saturday, September 12, 2026 at 6 PM

Location: Box 13 ArtSpace, 6700 Harrisburg Blvd., Houston, TX, 77011, United States

BOX 13 ArtSpace is pleased to present four new exhibitions opening Friday, September 11 , 2026 6–9 PM. BOX 13 ArtSpace is pleased to present in the Front BOX gallery: “Cryptic Bodies,” an exhibition of four interdisciplinary Houston-based femme artists who work in sculpture, collage, zines, and socially engaged practices. As one excavates their layered work, bodies are revealed, both human, non-human, touching upon women’s health, fragmentary memories, and interconnected ecosystems and identities. The exhibit in the Back gallery features Chris Ireland’s “Dead Letter Office,” which explores home, memory, and placelessness through carefully constructed collages that combine fragments from lived experience, online archives, real estate listings, and personal photographs. For “Mother Earth Weaves Infinite” in the Box 13 Window BOX Gallery, Cathie Kayser and Ellen H Ray use a variety of materials and techniques, including fabrics, mulberry silks, soft sculpture, paper mache, and wire and paper sculptures to present an immersive experience that highlights the complexity of the mycorrhizal network. With this work, the artists invite viewers to consider the interconnectedness of all living systems. The Earth, and the universe encompassing it, is a master plan of intelligent design that holds lessons for us about systems that work. Moving to our Upstairs BOX gallery we are excited to introduce “Grip Strength: An Army of Lovers Shall Not Fail” by KT Abadir-Mullally. Through interactive soft sculptures and ceramics inspired by strength sports and queer activism, the exhibition invites visitors to engage with themes of queer resilience, desire, collective power, and resistance. The exhibitions continue through October 10, 2026. An Opening Reception will be held on Friday, September 11, 2026, 6–9 PM at BOX 13 ArtSpace, 6700 Harrisburg, Houston, TX 77011. This event is funded in part by the City of Houston through the Houston Arts Alliance and Houston MOCA. Additional support is provided by The Brown Foundation, Saint Arnold Brewing Company, Giant Texas Distillers, JP Morgan – Nancy O’Connor Fund, and all who help make our programming possible.

From East End Farmers Market

item.title: Inprint Cool Brains! Series presents Rex Ogle
item.description:
Sunday, September 13, 2026 at 3 PM

Location: Meyerland Performing and Visual Arts Middle School, 10410 Manhattan Drive, Houston, TX, 77096, United States

Free and open to the public Free copies of one of Rex Ogle’s newest books for the first 100 families Presentation and Q&A by the author Meet the author followed by a book sale and signing Bus scholarships available for student groups – full scholarships for public schools, partial scholarships for private schools upon availability. For information, email info@inprint.org Discounted books available through Brazos Bookstore And more! The 2026/2027 Inprint Cool Brains! Series proudly presents award-winning author Rex Ogle, sharing his new books Fruitcake, a graphic novel about surviving middle school and finding the courage to be yourself, and Absent, a middle grade novel about three boys who skip school, told in verse, prose, and comics. Rex Ogle is the author of more than 100 books for kids, including comics, graphic novels, and memoirs—most notably Free Lunch (winner of the ALA/YALSA award for Excellence in Nonfiction), Abuela Don’t Forget Me (ALA/YALSA award for Excellence in Nonfiction finalist), Road Home (a Micheal Printz Honor and Stonewall Honor book), and middle grade graphic novels Four Eyes and Pizza Face. Under his pseudonym Rey Terciero, he has also reimagined classics as modern and diverse graphic novels, including Meg, Jo, Beth, & Amy, Northranger (nominated for both Harvey and GLAAD Media Awards), and Dan in Green Gables (nominated for a GLAAD Media Award). Born and raised in Texas, Rex now lives in Los Angeles where he writes every day—when he’s not reading X-Men, gaming with friends, or chasing his dog, Toby, trying to score a hug. Described as “funny, sad, goofy and poignant; a winner” (Kirkus starred review), Fruitcake is the third and final installment of Ogle’s highly popular Four Eyes graphic novel series, which tackles relatable middle school themes like bullying, puberty, building self-confidence, and navigating friendships. Eighth grade isn’t off to a great start for Rex. Everyone seems to be coupling up, and he’s starting to feel like an outsider—until he meets Charlotte. She’s fearless, smart, pretty, and, best of all, she likes him back. But as wonderful as Charlotte is, Rex can’t stop thinking about someone else: Drew, Rex’s childhood best friend. Suddenly, Rex is navigating feelings he never expected. With strong opinions swirling at home and church, Rex begins to question his own worth and what his feelings truly mean. Featuring Dave Valeza’s vibrant, colorful, and engaging illustrations, Fruitcake is a heartfelt story of laughter and fear, crushes and coming out, and the courage it takes to embrace who you are. With illustrations by LJ-Baptiste, Absent explores school absenteeism in a compelling, entertaining, and utterly distinct middle grade novel. With a dad in jail and a lack of teachers interested in helping him learn, Manny doesn’t see the point in anything besides skateboarding and writing lyrics. Calvin has so many responsibilities to his father and little brothers that when his bike is stolen, he can’t make it to school on time. And while Liam is studious and wants to become a doctor, he is tormented by bullies and hides out in an unused janitor’s closet instead of going to class. When the boys are thrown together in detention, they realize that they might still have a lot to learn—not just from their teachers, but from each other. Absent tells the boys’ stories in three distinct voices: Manny’s in verse, Calvin’s as a comic, and Liam’s as a prose journal. ***Please note that the book signing will be conducted on a first-come, first-served basis. Upon entering the theater, people wishing to have books signed will be given a number, and the book signing will take place in numerical order after the on-stage presentation.***

item.title: Inprint Claudia Rankine Reading
item.description:
Monday, September 14, 2026 at 7:30 PM

Location: Brockman Hall for Opera, Rice University, Entrance #18 off Rice Boulevard, Houston, TX, 77005

General admission tickets will go on sale on Tuesday, August 25, 2026 at 12 pm. Season tickets are on sale here. Claudia Rankine will read from her new hybrid-genre work Triage, followed by an on-stage conversation led by poet and Rice University professor Phillip B. Williams. The evening will conclude with a book sale and signing. The event is presented as part of the 2026/2027 Inprint Margarett Root Brown Reading Series.  Whether writing about intimacy or alienation, Claudia Rankine possesses a voice of unrelenting candor that “shimmers with wisdom and fury” (The Telegraph). A MacArthur Fellow, Rankine is the author of five collections of poetry, including her bestselling Citizen: An American Lyric, which explores what it means to be an American citizen in a “post-racial” society. A defining text for our time, Citizen won the National Book Critics Circle Award, the NAACP Image Award, the PEN Open Book Award, and the Los Angeles Times Book Prize. She is also the author of three plays, including Provenance of Beauty: A South Bronx Travelogue, which is performed on a bus ride through the Bronx; and is the editor of several anthologies, including The Racial Imaginary: Writers on Race in the Life of the Mind. Rankine returns to Inprint with her genre-defying new work Triage, which collides the lyric with narrative, memoir, image, and essay to offer her most personal and emotionally resonant writing yet. Triage follows the turbulent friendship between two characters, the narrator and the theorist, self-identified sisters struggling to define their wounded histories and their shared but separate lives. According to Jamaica Kincaid, “Claudia Rankine’s remarkable, outstanding odyssey—an account of our present, which is also our past, which is always our future—is beautifully rendered in a kaleidoscope of images and sensations. . . . Triage is exquisite.”

From Inprint Houston

item.title: National Voter Registration Day
item.description:
Tuesday, September 15, 2026 at 12 AM

Location: Houston Food Bank East Branch, 535 Portwall Street, Houston, TX, 77029, United States

Did you know that on Tuesday, September 15th, it’s National Voter Registration Day! At Houston Food Bank, we care about having your voice heard, and we are proud to provide the opportunity for you to register to vote on National Voter Registration Day! We are partnering with Harris County Tax Office and the National Voter Registration Day organization to serve as a site for Voter Registration at our Portwall location. You are eligible to register to vote if: You are a United States citizen; You are a resident of the county where you submit the application; You are at least 17 years and 10 months old on the date your voter registration application is submitted, and you are 18 years of age on Election Day. You are not a convicted felon (you may be eligible to vote if you have completed your sentence, probation, and parole); and You have not been declared by a court exercising probate jurisdiction to be either totally mentally incapacitated or partially mentally incapacitated without the right to vote. item.title: Latinos in Architecture: MaS
item.description:
Tuesday, September 15, 2026 at 7 PM

Location: Architecture Center Houston, 902 Commerce St., Houston, TX, 77002, United States

The Latinos in Architecture (LiA) collegiate Mentorship and Scholarship program (MaS), through AIA Houston and Architecture Center Houston, intends to bridge the gap between students and professionals in the Latino architecture community. The MaS program matches college students pursuing a career path in architecture with a mentor who has an established career in the field. The program is for Latino students who are striving to influence the future of the built environment and the architecture profession. MaS will kick off on September 15, 2026, and conclude in May 2027. PROGRAM ELIGIBILITYfor the mentorship: Students have the option to participate only in the mentorship program and not pursue the scholarship. But students are welcome to participate in any MaS-related events. Students pursuing a degree in architecture at the University of Houston, Rice University, or Prairie View A&M University. The program is open to both US citizens and foreign students. for the scholarship: Students with at least one more academic year to apply scholarship funds directly to tuition.  Students with full scholarships are not eligible. SCHOLARSHIP REQUIREMENTSThe 2026-2027 program starts in September 2026 and ends in May 2027. Regularly check in with an assigned mentor (at least 4 times). These meetings can be in-person, virtual, or via phone call.  ​Participate in the kick-off event where they will meet the mentors. Kick-off will take place September 15 at 7pm.  Participate in the portfolio review organized by the LiA Committee. Attend three LiA, AIAH, TSA or HNOMA-sponsored events. Not including student chapters or student-led events. Students are required to take a selfie at each event. Attend their university or college career fair. Submit a PDF on a project or portfolio at the end of the Fall semester. Submit a 5-minute video on a project or portfolio at the end of the Spring semester. The video should not be a recording of a class crit and should not exceed 5 minutes. AWARDS Students must participate in the listed activities to be considered for the scholarship. These activities are meant to support and complement the student’s academic career. Scholarships will be awarded based on student participation in the program and their end-of-semester submission, which will be reviewed by a jury. 

From AIA Houston

For children 0 – 18 months and their caregivers Babies in nature? Babies ARE nature! Babies who spend time outside are stronger, healthier, more confident, and better sleepers. Learn how to support your Hatchlings as they develop motor skills, test physical limits, cultivate their sense of wonder, and get messy in a safe place to try new things. Hatchlings will engage in outdoor nature play in this unique opportunity to interact, explore, and bond with their caregivers in the natural world. This program will be held outdoors and will include loose parts and messy play with natural sensory elements such as sand, mud, grass, sticks, leaves, and water. Space is limited and pre-registration is required for all Hatchlings classes. Select Wednesdays from 10:00 am – 11:00 am. item.title: Unified Topgolf Pro-Am (Houston-Katy)
item.description:
Friday, September 18, 2026 at 10 AM

Location: Topgolf-Katy, 1030 Memorial Brook Blvd, Houston, TX 77084, Houston, 77084

The Unified Topgolf Pro-Am is one of the most exciting and meaningful community partnership events hosted by Special Olympics Texas, bringing together athletes, families, coaches, volunteers, corporate partners, and local business leaders for an unforgettable day of golf, laughter, connection, and community impact. Each bay includes a Special Olympics Texas athlete paired alongside five golfers, creating a truly unique experience where relationships, memories, and meaningful moments are built throughout the day. From friendly competition and team spirit to incredible conversations and shared experiences, the event is designed to bring people together in a fun and welcoming environment while directly supporting local athletes and programs. Proceeds from the Unified Topgolf Pro-Am help provide year-round sports training, competitions, health initiatives, leadership development, and educational opportunities for children, teenagers, and adults with intellectual disabilities throughout the greater Houston area. As the event continues growing each year, the Unified Topgolf Pro-Am has quickly become a tremendous opportunity for organizations and community members to make a real impact while being part of something incredibly energetic, uplifting, and memorable. For more information regarding sponsorship opportunities, team entries, volunteer involvement, or sponsorship opportunities, please reach out to Jared Kossover, Strategic Partnerships Manager with Special Olympics Texas Jared Kossover E: jkossover@sotx.org C: 737-867-9659

item.title: September 11 – October 10, 2026 Exhibitions
item.description:
Friday, September 18, 2026 at 6 PM

Location: Box 13 ArtSpace, 6700 Harrisburg Blvd., Houston, TX, 77011, United States

BOX 13 ArtSpace is pleased to present four new exhibitions opening Friday, September 11 , 2026 6–9 PM. BOX 13 ArtSpace is pleased to present in the Front BOX gallery: “Cryptic Bodies,” an exhibition of four interdisciplinary Houston-based femme artists who work in sculpture, collage, zines, and socially engaged practices. As one excavates their layered work, bodies are revealed, both human, non-human, touching upon women’s health, fragmentary memories, and interconnected ecosystems and identities. The exhibit in the Back gallery features Chris Ireland’s “Dead Letter Office,” which explores home, memory, and placelessness through carefully constructed collages that combine fragments from lived experience, online archives, real estate listings, and personal photographs. For “Mother Earth Weaves Infinite” in the Box 13 Window BOX Gallery, Cathie Kayser and Ellen H Ray use a variety of materials and techniques, including fabrics, mulberry silks, soft sculpture, paper mache, and wire and paper sculptures to present an immersive experience that highlights the complexity of the mycorrhizal network. With this work, the artists invite viewers to consider the interconnectedness of all living systems. The Earth, and the universe encompassing it, is a master plan of intelligent design that holds lessons for us about systems that work. Moving to our Upstairs BOX gallery we are excited to introduce “Grip Strength: An Army of Lovers Shall Not Fail” by KT Abadir-Mullally. Through interactive soft sculptures and ceramics inspired by strength sports and queer activism, the exhibition invites visitors to engage with themes of queer resilience, desire, collective power, and resistance. The exhibitions continue through October 10, 2026. An Opening Reception will be held on Friday, September 11, 2026, 6–9 PM at BOX 13 ArtSpace, 6700 Harrisburg, Houston, TX 77011. This event is funded in part by the City of Houston through the Houston Arts Alliance and Houston MOCA. Additional support is provided by The Brown Foundation, Saint Arnold Brewing Company, Giant Texas Distillers, JP Morgan – Nancy O’Connor Fund, and all who help make our programming possible.

From East End Farmers Market
